_comment: Roadmap VX11's cross-platform bitstream-hash gate - see tools/checks/check_cross_platform_hash.py for what this pins and why. Key: '<kernels-line-from-ac3cli--version>/<fast|reference>/<ac3|eac3|eac3_cpl>'. Value: SHA-256 of the matching file (gold.ac3/gold.ec3/gold_cpl.ec3) verify_gold_reference.sh's own encode step produces from tests/golden/audio/reference_51.wav. x86_64-sse2 and generic are measured directly (WSL2, GCC 16, real x86-64 hardware). aarch64-neon is measured on the REAL arm64 CI legs (PR #503, CI run 33635430769: linux-gcc-arm64, linux-llvm-arm64, windows-msvc-arm64, macos-llvm), not from the qemu cross-build this file previously declined to pre-fill from - and it comes back byte-identical to x86_64-sse2 on all three streams. That is the finding, not a formality: this project's ENCODER is bit-exact across architectures, so the ~6.02 dB gold-reference gap the arm64 legs measure is entirely decode-side. macOS x64 shares the x86_64-sse2 kernel and pins against it. Add any future leg's pin from its own CI run's 'unpinned' log lines. The encfloat mode is the float ENCODE path (AC3FORGE_ENCODE_SCALAR=float, the minimum-footprint profile's encoder on a hosted target): a different, equally valid stream from the same programme, pinned from the linux-gcc leg's own run and identical to MSVC's on the same kernel (2026-09-10). The E-AC-3 pins moved on 2026-09-10 with the rate-control search's warm start: the frame's mantissa cost is not monotone in the SNR offset (src/forge/src/encoder/snr_search.hpp), so the probe sequence decides which fitting boundary a rare frame lands on, and a search that starts each of its two passes from its own previous answer lands differently. x86_64-sse2 and generic were measured (MSVC and Linux GCC agree); aarch64-neon carries the same value on the strength of the encoder's measured bit-exactness across architectures, and the arm64 legs' own run is what confirms it.
